primary_claim: Synthetic scalable oversight -- training tiny (under 10,000-parameter) graph-neural-network agents inside statistically-calibrated abstract graphical models of real-world debate/collaboration problems, rather than full LLMs -- lets researchers evaluate and black-box-search over oversight/debate protocols cheaply and at arbitrary problem sizes; a SHADE-based search over ~4000 candidate collaboration mechanisms for a synthetic Lean-theorem-proving multi-agent environment found a learned mechanism that outperforms hand-crafted baselines (collaborative team rewards, a prediction market, and a blanket per-proof bounty) at solving targeted theorems.

effect.metric: time-discounted number of targeted theorems solved by agents trained under different collaboration mechanisms
effect.value: the SHADE-searched learned mechanism outperforms hand-crafted baselines (collaborative team reward, prediction market, blanket bounty) at solving targeted theorems in the synthetic math environment, found via a search over ~4000 candidate mechanisms (3 state dims, 2 signal-action dims, 6 environment dims)

stated_future_work: Build a synthetic debate-style environment that reproduces natural-language debate protocol rankings, to verify synthetic evaluation matches real evaluation where natural-language rankings are available
Iterate on each step of the synthetics pipeline (graphical model choice, environment distribution, training pipeline, mechanism parameterization) for debate-style problems
Establish standard synthetic environments for major problems of interest as a community resource

Prove theoretical scaling bounds (e.g. inverse-polynomial or exponential decay in debate length T) for protocol accuracy under fixed random-graph distributions, building on empirically-validated realistic graph distributions
Investigate whether there are theoretical or philosophical reasons debates or proofs should follow a particular random-graph distribution
Interpret the learned (SHADE-found) collaboration mechanisms, which are not easily interpretable

Pair synthetic-trained actor networks with real LLMs performing the underlying actions (prove/conjecture/estimate) as the ultimate indicator of a synthetic model's accuracy, not yet tested for mathematics
limitations_stated: Making the random graph distribution over problems realistic is described as the hardest and most important part of synthetics; both dataset-calibration and LLM-elicitation approaches to setting it have real biases and are not obviously sufficient
The synthetic mathematics model has not yet been verified by pairing synthetics-trained actor networks with real LLMs in the wild
The learned collaboration mechanism found via SHADE search is not easily interpretable
The synthetic model of mathematics is not claimed to be optimal, only illustrative of what is possible; many alternative graphical-model design choices were considered but not adopted
quote: In a search over approximately 4000 mechanisms (3 state dimensions, 2 signal action dimensions, 6 environment dimensions), we found a mechanism that beat our hand-crafted baselines.
